name: logan_paul_best_video
summary: An educational video essay breaking down narrative rhythm and contrast in video editing. The style features talking-head analysis intercut with NLE timeline screenshots, diagrammatic scribbles, and dynamic pacing shifts.

captions.notes: Minimal dialogue captions used primarily for quoting source footage or key punchlines with clean drop shadows.

headline.notes: Large distressed white uppercase typography introduces major concepts like CONTRAST EDITING and RHYTHM across split backgrounds.

callouts.notes: White hand-drawn digital scribbles, story arc lines, and timeline bracket annotations explain pacing structure.

transitions.notes: Sharp hard cuts dominate, paired with deliberate sound design drops and sudden audio swells.

rules: Anchor theoretical editing lessons with immediate source footage demonstrations.
Display timeline UI directly beneath footage to visualize audio and cut density.
Use hand-drawn animated white graphs to visualize narrative tension arcs.
Contrast fast-paced montage sequences with prolonged uninterrupted dialogue cuts.
Cut audio completely for punchy naked talking head segments.
Pair thematic shifts with dramatic musical swells and sudden breaks.
Label temporal milestones and average cut durations with clear text overlays.
Vary cut duration across scenes to create distinct rhythm and emotional variety
Display editing timelines beneath footage to directly demonstrate structural choices
Use hand-drawn narrative curves to map rising and falling emotional tension
Cut on musical beats during fast sequences, but hold long takes during climax moments
Use music swells and sudden music cutouts to accentuate story shifts
avoid: Static talking-head shots exceeding five seconds without punch-ins.
Flashing rainbow caption animations or karaoke text pills.
Generic stock wipes or artificial transition effects.
Constant hyperactive fast-cutting without breathing room
Distracting animated caption presets or karaoke highlighting
Flashy transitional effects like digital glitches or whip zooms
Crowding the screen with unnecessary stickers or emojis
